items.where: plan/DECISIONS.md D-090 (state text by std::to_chars/std::from_chars) vs plan/ci/ci.yml jobs plugins (Configure on macOS: -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0) and core (macos-15, macos-15-intel); S-110, S-320
items.text: Apple's libc++ makes floating-point std::to_chars unavailable below macOS 13.3, so the core (folkdsp is built inside the plugins configure) cannot compile with the plugins job's deployment target 11.0. The Xcode 16 libc++ on the macos-15 images also has no floating-point std::from_chars, so the core job fails on both macOS runners too. D-090 forbids every alternative (printf, strtod, streams), DR-14 excludes failures caused by the plan's code, and ENVIRONMENT section 5 does not list the item as unverified, so the implementer is stuck at S-320 with no rule.
items.suggested_fix: Either let D-090 use a locale-independent fallback (for example streams imbued with std::locale::classic(), or a hand-written shortest round-trip formatter and parser) when floating-point to_chars/from_chars is unavailable, or raise the deployment target and name a toolchain that provides both; then add the item to the unverified table of ENVIRONMENT section 5 with an 'If it fails' rule.

items.where: plan/DECISIONS.md D-053 (void if one letter for 10 or more of the 14), plan/GATES.md G-L1 to G-L5, S-340 score_gate.py, S-LISTEN action 1 (seed = round number)
items.text: In tools/listening/make_blind_pairs.py the sequence of sides depends only on the seed, not on the stems. With 14 pairs, seed 2 gives the key BBBBABBBBABBAB (11 B), and seeds 3 and 6 give 10 B. A listener who identifies every pair correctly therefore gives 10 or more of one letter, and score_gate.py must call the round void. That hides exactly the failing result (more than 8 of 12 correct) that the gate exists to catch, and S-LISTEN's round 2 uses seed 2. About 18 % of seeds are affected.
items.suggested_fix: Define the side-bias rule relative to the key (void only if the answers have 10 or more of one letter while the key does not), or have build_evidence reject or redraw any seed whose key has 10 or more of one side, and state which in D-053 and S-340.

items.where: plan/PLAN.md S-LISTEN actions 1, 4 and 5; plan/DECISIONS.md D-053; plan/GATES.md G-L branches
items.text: The marker uses seed=<round number>, but a void round is repeated 'with a new seed' and 'is not a round of the limit', so the round number, and with it the seed and the record name (GATE-<id>-r<N>.md, listening/<id>-round-<N>.md), is undefined for the repeat. After two void rounds in a row 'the record asks the owner how to continue', but no allowed responses are defined for that question.
items.suggested_fix: Give a seed rule independent of the round number (for example a running attempt counter recorded in the gate file), a file name for void attempts, and the allowed responses after two void rounds.

items.text: key.json.b64 holds only the side of each pair. Which pairs are the controls (stems control-1 and control-2) is recorded only in sources.json.b64, which score_gate.py's interface does not take, yet the tool must report the control results and the score over the 12 real pairs.
items.suggested_fix: Add --sources <sources.json.b64> to score_gate.py (or say it reads the sibling file) in S-340 and S-LISTEN action 5.

items.where: plan/PLAN.md S-340 action 1(c) (MANIFEST.json derived_from for pair clips); plan/DECISIONS.md D-053 (listener not told which pairs are controls)
items.text: Each pair clip's derived_from is 'the id of that pair's reference'. On the public evidence branch this reveals the note behind every pair, which the pair builder deliberately keeps base64-encoded, and the two ids that appear twice point to the four pairs among which the controls sit.
items.suggested_fix: List the ids of all 12 references in derived_from for every pair clip, as is already done for key.json.b64, which still satisfies the guard.

items.where: plan/DECISIONS.md D-094 and plan/PLAN.md S-310 action 2 (temporary engine per getStateInformation and setStateInformation); tests/juce/host_test.cpp T-304 (more than 100 calls in 5 s); plan/ci/ci.yml host-tsan
items.text: Nothing says whether the temporary engine must be prepared, or whether setParam, saveState and loadState work on an unprepared engine. prepare() builds 85 x 2048 useful-section tables per reed instrument (five sets for the melodion). An implementer who prepares the temporary engine, three per iteration, risks missing T-304's 100 calls in 5 s under ThreadSanitizer.
items.suggested_fix: State in D-090/D-094 that create, setParam, getParam, saveState and loadState are valid before prepare() and that the wrapper's temporary engine is never prepared.

items.where: plan/ci/gate-evidence.yml job publish, step 'Pushed branch holds the bundle'; plan/DECISIONS.md D-084; HANDOFF.md 'Delivering audio'
items.text: The verification runs an unauthenticated git fetch from https://github.com/<repo>.git. It fails on a private repository, which the plan explicitly allows once the owner confirms the Actions budget, so every gate-evidence run would end red after a successful push.
items.suggested_fix: Fetch with the same x-access-token URL as the push, or verify with git ls-remote using the token.

items.text: The stores are cloned with git clone --depth 1, then git diff --stat 9934bb5 HEAD -- scripts/ (and f3d176d) is required before running their scripts. Those commits are not present in a depth-1 clone, so the diff fails and the precondition cannot be evaluated.
items.suggested_fix: Clone without --depth, or add git fetch --depth=1 origin 9934bb5 (f3d176d) before the diff.

items.where: tests/py/test_fetch_references.py test_T211_archive_hash_is_checked_before_extraction (subprocess timeout 120 s); plan/DECISIONS.md D-052; plan/PLAN.md S-REF action 5 ('exit 1 on any mismatch or failed download after 3 attempts')
items.text: No decision says whether a cached archive whose sha256 differs from archives.csv is refused at once or re-downloaded, nor what retry delays apply. An implementer who re-downloads with DR-01-style waits (30, 60, 120 s) against example.invalid exceeds the test's 120 s timeout, and T-211 fails.
items.suggested_fix: State in D-052 that a cached archive with a wrong hash is refused immediately (exit 1, no download), and give short bounded retry delays for real downloads.

items.where: plan/PLAN.md S-REVIEW On failure and S-ADVERSARIAL On failure vs their Actions and Gate lines and plan/GATES.md G-004
items.text: Actions and Gate say an unfixable Critical or High finding opens G-004 for the owner's accept, fix or stop. S-REVIEW's On failure says it 'halts the plan with BLOCKED.md', and S-ADVERSARIAL's says such breaks block S-LISTEN until fixed, with no mention of an accept.
items.suggested_fix: Make both On failure lines say 'open G-004; BLOCKED.md only on a stop response'.

items.where: plan/DECISIONS.md D-090 (the wrapper's editor states the unsupported rate in one line) vs D-094 (returns a juce::GenericAudioProcessorEditor; a custom editor is not required)
items.text: A bare GenericAudioProcessorEditor cannot show an extra line of text, so the two decisions conflict about what createEditor returns.
items.suggested_fix: Say the editor is a small component holding the generic editor plus one label, or drop the text line from D-090.

items.text: Question 4 checks the shipped plugins in the owner's host (wheel, breath CC, preset load, session reopen). The allowed responses and the iterate branch (DR-12, the listening iterate procedure) cover sound only, so a functional defect reported here has no route back to S-310/S-320 or to the other four plugins.
items.suggested_fix: Add a branch: a question-4 defect is fixed in the wrapper, S-310 and S-320 are re-verified, and the question is asked again in the next G-L1 round.

items.text: The 'If it fails' column covers only TSan reports inside JUCE. A ThreadSanitizer that aborts at start-up on the runner kernel ('unexpected memory mapping' with high vm.mmap_rnd_bits) is not covered, and the job would then fail at its test step exactly as S-003 expects, which hides the cause.
items.suggested_fix: Add a row (fix: sudo sysctl vm.mmap_rnd_bits=28 or run under setarch -R, logged as a deviation), and have S-003 check the job log for a T-304 Catch2 summary rather than only reaching the step.

items.where: plan/DECISIONS.md D-084 budget; plan/PLAN.md S-000 action 5 (private repository: owner confirms the Actions budget)
items.text: The per-push budget (about 150 runner-minutes) lists core, plugins, reference, freeze and audit but not the new host-tsan job, a full JUCE build with ThreadSanitizer, so the figure the owner would confirm is understated.
items.suggested_fix: Add host-tsan to the D-084 estimate.

items.where: plan/PLAN.md S-110 Done when ($B/folk-locale-tests exits 0); plan/ENVIRONMENT.md section 2 (locale-gen as root); DR-10, DR-13
items.text: T-016 fails, never skips, without a comma locale. In a sandbox without root (S-000 action 4: DR-10), de_DE.UTF-8 cannot be generated. DR-10 still tells the implementer to test the core locally, and DR-13 covers only recycling or network, so S-110's Done when cannot be met and no rule names CI as the evaluator.
items.suggested_fix: Extend DR-13 (or DR-10) to a missing locale: the core job's 'Locale tests (T-016)' step is then the evidence.

items.where: plan/PLAN.md S-REF action 5 option list and Done when; plan/DECISIONS.md D-052
items.text: S-REF lists the tool's options as --index, --root, --archive-cache and --only-redistributable, without --archives (which T-211 passes). D-052 gives no default for --archive-cache, which S-REF's Done-when command and S-LISTEN omit, though the cache must lie outside the repository.
items.suggested_fix: Add --archives to S-REF's list and give --archive-cache a default outside the working tree (for example $HOME/folk-ref-archives).

items.where: plan/TRACEABILITY.md section 3 and 'Required categories'; HANDOFF.md section 3 (frozen suite)
items.text: The decision-to-test table maps D-052 only to T-200, T-201 and T-210, and D-090 to D-094 only to T-008, T-014, T-160 to T-163 and T-302. It omits T-016, T-211, T-303 and T-304. HANDOFF section 3 lists the frozen suite without folk-locale-tests.
items.suggested_fix: Add the four tests to TRACEABILITY sections 2B and 3 and add folk-locale-tests to HANDOFF section 3.

items.text: The sentence 'which the wrapper strips before loadState and restores and restores it only if loadState accepts it' is garbled. It does not say what happens to a blob with no #program line or with an index outside the factory list (is it refused, or is the state loaded with the program left as it was?).
items.suggested_fix: Rewrite it: the last line, if it is '#program <i>' with a valid i, is removed and stored as the current program after loadState accepts the rest; otherwise the whole blob goes to loadState and the program is unchanged.

steps_walked: T-302 locale, program and sample-rate cases
TRACEABILITY counts (27 Catch2, 2 locale, 9 per host program, 316 pytest, 16 reference, 7 ctest)
summary:
Counts agree across files: 27 + 2 Catch2 cases, 9 host cases per plugin, 316/14 pytest, T-211 = 10, ctest 7, 14 pairs / 28 clips.
Blocker 1: D-090's mandated to_chars/from_chars for floats cannot compile on the macOS runners (deployment target 11.0 in the plugins job; no float from_chars in the Xcode 16 libc++), and no rule covers it.
Blocker 2: D-053's side-bias void rule voids a perfectly correct answer set whenever the key itself has 10 or more of one side (seeds 2, 3, 6; round 2 uses seed 2), hiding a failing gate.
Guesses: seeding and allowed responses after void rounds; the cost of the temporary engine under TSan; an unauthenticated fetch in publish on a private repository; a depth-1 clone that cannot diff old commits in S-KNOW; T-211 timeout versus retry policy.
Minor: G-004 versus BLOCKED wording, editor text versus generic editor, G-L1 question 4 branch, TSan start-up rule, budget, locale without root, fetch options, traceability gaps, the garbled #program sentence.
